groups.reason: Both are serializer-side checks requiring UncompressedPointRepresentation.Y to contain exactly coordinate_length opaque octets. The canonical member has the clearer explicit serialization condition and primary-body evidence.

This member covers encoding and parsing and additionally checks that legacy_record_version follows type, including field order and width. Those parser and position constraints are absent from the other member.
This member only states the encoding type of TLSPlaintext.legacy_record_version and does not independently impose the other member's parser-direction and field-position checks.
This requirement is expressly limited to encoding OfferedPsks.binders within the 33-through-2^16-1 vector bounds.
This is an unconditioned structural limit applicable to the OfferedPsks.binders wire field, including parser acceptance, so it is broader in implementation direction than the encoding-only member.
Both apply to inbound unknown alert types and require the same fatal error-alert treatment in TLS 1.3. The canonical member supplies the direct normative MUST from the primary Alert Protocol text.

Both are encoding checks requiring the ClientHello EarlyDataIndication variant to have an Empty extension body. The canonical member states the zero-payload consequence explicitly and cites the primary-body definition.

Both require the uniform bad_record_mac outcome for every received-record decryption or deprotection failure, without distinguishable failure alerts. The canonical member cites the direct primary-body alert definition.
This is an unconditioned structural limit on the PskKeyExchangeModes.ke_modes wire field, including parser acceptance.
This member checks only encoding ke_modes within the 1-through-255-octet bounds, so its implementation direction is narrower than the unconditioned structural member.

Both constrain serializer and parser handling of ServerHello.extensions to an encoded vector length of 6 through 2^16-1 octets. The canonical member makes both directions explicit and uses primary-body evidence.
Both require the client to encode obfuscated_ticket_age as ticket age plus ticket_age_add modulo 2^32. The canonical member gives the complete field formula, including the millisecond unit, directly.
This member checks the concrete Finished.verify_data formula: HMAC with finished_key over the transcript hash with optional Certificate and CertificateVerify inputs.

This member separately requires the Finished MAC key to be derived from the applicable Base Key and states the MAC operation more abstractly. That key-provenance check is not the same atomic check as merely using finished_key in the concrete formula.
Both require encoding and decoding KeyUpdateRequest.update_not_requested as numeric value 0. The canonical member uses the direct primary-body enum definition.
Both require encoding and decoding SignatureScheme.ecdsa_secp521r1_sha512 as code point 0x0603. The canonical member cites the primary-body definition.
Both require encoding and interpreting CertificateType.RawPublicKey as wire value 2. The canonical member is the direct primary-body definition.
This member checks only serializer output: TLSCiphertext.encrypted_record contains exactly TLSCiphertext.length octets.
This member covers both encoding and parsing and additionally requires encrypted_record to follow the length field, so its direction and field-order scope exceed the encoding-only length check.
